measures.title: Santa Fe County Road Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether Santa Fe County may issue up to $14,035,000 in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes. The money would be used to acquire, build, design, equip and improve roads within the county.
measures.yesMeans: The county may issue up to $14,035,000 in property-tax-backed bonds for roads.
measures.noMeans: The county may not issue these road bonds.

measures.title: Santa Fe County Water and Wastewater Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether Santa Fe County may issue up to $6,500,000 in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes. The money would be used to acquire real property and needed water rights for, and to build, design, equip, rehabilitate and improve, water and wastewater projects within the county.
measures.yesMeans: The county may issue up to $6,500,000 in property-tax-backed bonds for water and wastewater projects.
measures.noMeans: The county may not issue these water and wastewater bonds.

measures.title: Santa Fe County Open Space, Trails and Parks Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether Santa Fe County may issue up to $7,010,000 in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes. The money would be used to acquire, design, build, improve, equip and restore open space, trails and parks within the county.
measures.yesMeans: The county may issue up to $7,010,000 in property-tax-backed bonds for open space, trails and parks.
measures.noMeans: The county may not issue these open space, trails and parks bonds.

measures.title: Santa Fe County Fire Station Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether Santa Fe County may issue up to $17,455,000 in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes. The money would be used to acquire real property for, and to build, design, equip, rehabilitate and improve, fire stations within the county.
measures.yesMeans: The county may issue up to $17,455,000 in property-tax-backed bonds for fire stations.
measures.noMeans: The county may not issue these fire station bonds.

measures.id: General Obligation Street, Sidewalk, and Pedestrian Accessibility Bonds
measures.title: General Obligation Street, Sidewalk, and Pedestrian Accessibility Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether the City of Santa Fe may issue up to $11,250,000 in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes. The money would be used to plan, design, build, rehabilitate, repair, replace and improve streets, sidewalks, curb ramps, pedestrian routes and related infrastructure within the city.
measures.yesMeans: The city may issue up to $11,250,000 in property-tax-backed bonds for streets, sidewalks and pedestrian access.
measures.noMeans: The city may not issue these street and sidewalk bonds.

measures.id: General Obligation Municipal Recreation Complex Soccer Valley Bonds
measures.title: General Obligation Municipal Recreation Complex Soccer Valley Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether the City of Santa Fe may issue up to $4,500,000 in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes. The money would be used to plan, design, build, equip, furnish, improve and expand athletic fields and related public recreational facilities and infrastructure at the Municipal Recreation Complex Soccer Valley.
measures.yesMeans: The city may issue up to $4,500,000 in property-tax-backed bonds for the Municipal Recreation Complex Soccer Valley.
measures.noMeans: The city may not issue these Soccer Valley bonds.

measures.id: General Obligation SWAN Park Improvement Bonds
measures.title: General Obligation SWAN Park Improvement Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether the City of Santa Fe may issue up to $4,250,000 in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes. The money would be used to plan, design, build, equip, furnish and improve a splash pad and related public recreational facilities and infrastructure at SWAN Park.
measures.yesMeans: The city may issue up to $4,250,000 in property-tax-backed bonds for SWAN Park improvements.
measures.noMeans: The city may not issue these SWAN Park bonds.

measures.id: General Obligation Midtown Capital Improvement Bonds
measures.title: General Obligation Midtown Capital Improvement Bonds
measures.summary: Asks whether the City of Santa Fe may issue up to $5,000,000 in general obligation bonds, repaid from property taxes. The money would be used to plan, design, prepare, demolish, build, renovate, equip, furnish, manage and improve public facilities, infrastructure, public spaces and other City-owned assets at the Midtown property.
measures.yesMeans: The city may issue up to $5,000,000 in property-tax-backed bonds for the Midtown property.
measures.noMeans: The city may not issue these Midtown bonds.
